heuristics: r-adding walks on the six-element GLV-negation classes behave as random mappings on N'=(r-1)/6 orbits, so a collision among K class evaluations has probability 1-exp(-K^2/(2N')) (Teske; van Oorschot-Wiener; Bernstein-Lange-Schwabe).

With R=2048 partitions, look-ahead and periodic 2/4-cycle escape, fruitless-cycle and r-adding overhead is covered by running 1.25 K steps; this 25% allowance is extrapolated from published moderate-scale measurements, not a production-size experiment.
limitations: Analytic construction with a stated random-walk heuristic; no full-size execution or independent qualification.
